practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary official definition of a Non-Resident Indian (NRI) under the Indian Income Tax Act?
opts: An Indian citizen who stays abroad for employment or business for any length of time.
An Indian citizen who resides outside India for less than 182 days in a financial year.
Any person holding a Foreign passport of Indian origin.
A person born in undivided India who later migrated.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the Income Tax Act, an NRI is an Indian citizen who is not a 'resident' of India. A resident is someone who stays in India for 182 days or more in a financial year. If they stay for less than 182 days, they are considered NRIs for tax purposes.

practiceQuestions.q: The Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD) is celebrated biennially on which date to mark the contribution of the overseas Indian community?
practiceQuestions.sol: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas is celebrated on 9th January every year (now held biennially) to commemorate the return of Mahatma Gandhi from South Africa to Mumbai in 1915.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following constitutional articles deals with the rights of citizenship of certain persons of Indian origin residing outside India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 8 of the Indian Constitution grants citizenship rights to certain persons of Indian origin residing outside India, provided either their parents or grandparents were born in undivided India.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'Persons of Indian Origin' (PIO) card scheme was merged into which scheme in the year 2015?
opts: Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Card Scheme
practiceQuestions.sol: In January 2015, the Government of India merged the PIO card scheme with the OCI card scheme to eliminate confusion and streamline benefits for people of Indian origin.

practiceQuestions.q: Which ministry is the nodal ministry for handling matters related to Overseas Indians and the Indian Diaspora?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs (MOIA) was merged with the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) in 2016. Currently, the MEA acts as the nodal ministry for all diaspora-related matters.

practiceQuestions.q: What does 'OCI' stand for in the context of the Indian diaspora?
practiceQuestions.sol: OCI stands for Overseas Citizen of India. It is a lifelong visa status granted to eligible foreign citizens of Indian origin.

practiceQuestions.q: The concept of 'Girmitiyas' is historically associated with which wave of the Indian diaspora migration?
opts: Post-independence professional migration to North America
Recent Gulf migration of blue-collar workers
Ancient trade expansion into Southeast Asia
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Girmitiyas' (derived from the word 'agreement') refers to indentured laborers transported under British colonial rule to work on sugar plantations in Fiji, Mauritius, Caribbean, etc.

practiceQuestions.q: Which amendment to the Representation of the People Act, 1950, enabled overseas Indian citizens to register as voters in their constituencies in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 2010 inserted Section 20A, allowing Indian citizens residing abroad due to employment or education to register as electors in India.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary objective of the 'VAJRA' faculty scheme launched by the Government of India regarding the diaspora?
opts: To bring overseas Indian scientists and academicians to work in Indian public institutions temporarily.
To provide insurance cover to blue-collar workers in Gulf countries.
To facilitate voting rights for NRIs via postal ballot.
To grant dual citizenship to persons of Indian origin in western nations.
practiceQuestions.sol: VAJRA (Visiting Advanced Joint Research) faculty scheme enables Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs) to conduct research in Indian public funded institutions.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the Indian Constitution, can an OCI cardholder contest elections to the Parliament or State Legislature of India?
opts: Yes, after obtaining special permission from the Election Commission.
Yes, if they hold a valid Indian passport.
No, OCI cardholders do not have voting rights or the right to contest elections.
Only for local body elections like Panchayats and Municipalities.
practiceQuestions.sol: OCI cardholders are foreign citizens. They do not enjoy political rights in India, meaning they cannot vote in elections, contest elections, or hold constitutional posts such as President, MP, or MLA.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the economic engagement of the Indian diaspora in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries structurally differ from that in Western nations like the US and UK?
opts: GCC diaspora mostly consists of high-skilled professionals who own large corporations, whereas Western diaspora comprises blue-collar workers.

GCC diaspora is primarily semi-skilled/blue-collar with high remittance flows and temporary residency, while Western diaspora is high-skilled, permanent settlers with significant philanthropic and investment contributions.
There is no structural difference; both regions export identical proportions of IT professionals and manual laborers.
GCC diaspora enjoys full political citizenship rights, whereas Western diaspora has zero economic ties with India.
practiceQuestions.sol: The diaspora in the Gulf is largely contractual, comprising semi-skilled and unskilled workers who send massive remittances back home but rarely attain permanent citizenship. In contrast, Western diasporas are predominantly high-skilled professionals who have integrated locally, acquired citizenship, and now wield considerable soft power and venture capital influence in India.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary rationale behind India's policy shift from opposing dual citizenship to creating the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) framework?
opts: To comply with international human rights laws mandated by the United Nations.
To harness the brain drain into 'brain gain' by engaging wealthy and skilled diaspora without constitutional contradictions of political dual citizenship.
To allow diaspora members to vote in Indian general elections without residing in India.
To collect direct taxes from foreign nationals of Indian origin.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 9 of the Indian Constitution strictly prohibits single citizens holding multiple nationalities. To bypass this while leveraging the economic, technological, and intellectual capital of the affluent diaspora, India introduced the OCI scheme, which offers lifelong economic, commercial, and educational rights without political franchise.

practiceQuestions.q: How does 'Soft Power' diplomacy manifest through the Indian diaspora in contemporary international relations?
opts: By exerting military pressure on host nations through diaspora-run defense contractors.
Through cultural diffusion, propagation of yoga, festivals, electoral lobbying, and influencing foreign policy decisions favorable to India in host parliaments.
By replacing local political systems in Western countries with Indian democratic governance models.
Solely through the transfer of remittances to mitigate India's current account deficit.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Indian diaspora acts as cultural ambassadors and effective pressure groups. Their success in fields like science, politics, and business elevates India's global stature, shapes favorable geopolitical narratives, and enables strategic lobbying (e.g., during the India-US Civil Nuclear Deal).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary significance of Remittances sent by the Indian diaspora to the macroeconomic stability of India?
opts: They form the primary source of tax revenue for the Union Government.
They finance India's trade deficit, stabilize the current account, and provide crucial liquidity for household consumption and poverty alleviation.
They directly control the repo rate and monetary policy formulated by the Reserve Bank of India.
They act as sovereign foreign direct investment (FDI) controlled by foreign central banks.
practiceQuestions.sol: India is consistently the top recipient of remittances globally (exceeding $100 billion annually). These non-debt creating foreign inflows help bridge the country's trade deficit, support foreign exchange reserves, and boost domestic consumption.

practiceQuestions.q: How has the nature of the Indian diaspora evolved from the 19th century to the 21st century?
opts: From high-tech professionals to indentured agricultural manual laborers.
From colonial-era indentured and manual labor to post-independence professional/technical migration, and further to contemporary digital, startup, and entrepreneurial diaspora.
From political refugees fleeing partition to government-mandated forced displacement.
The diaspora composition has remained completely static throughout history.
practiceQuestions.sol: The diaspora evolution spans three distinct phases: Phase 1 (Colonial indenture labor to plantations), Phase 2 (Post-colonial 'brain drain' of doctors, engineers, and scientists to the West and Gulf), and Phase 3 (Contemporary tech entrepreneurs, venture capitalists, and global corporate leaders).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary legal and operational challenge regarding voting rights for Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) living abroad?
opts: Lack of internet infrastructure in Indian embassies.
The mandatory requirement under current laws to cast votes physically in person at their respective polling booths in India.
Total refusal of the Election Commission to register NRIs on electoral rolls.
Prohibition of dual nationality for OCI cardholders.
practiceQuestions.sol: While the 2010 amendment allowed NRIs to register as voters, Section 20 of the RP Act, 1950 requires them to vote in person at their designated polling booth in India. Proposals for proxy voting or postal ballots are still under legislative debate due to logistical and security complexities.

practiceQuestions.q: How do Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs) differ fundamentally from Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) in terms of legal status?
opts: NRIs are foreign passport holders, whereas OCIs hold Indian passports.
NRIs are Indian citizens living abroad temporarily, whereas OCIs are foreign citizens of Indian origin granted lifelong multi-entry visa privileges.
OCIs have full voting rights in Indian Lok Sabha elections, while NRIs do not.
There is no legal difference; both terms are used interchangeably by the Ministry of Home Affairs.
practiceQuestions.sol: NRIs remain citizens of India holding an Indian passport, subject to Indian income tax laws based on residency. OCIs are foreign nationals (holding foreign passports) who are granted a lifetime visa status to reside, work, and study in India, with certain restrictions like needing special permission for missionary or research work.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the strategic significance of the 'Pravasi Bharatiya Kendra' (now Sushma Swaraj Bhawan) established in New Delhi?
opts: It serves as a detention camp for illegal immigrants deported from Western countries.
It acts as a institutional hub and resource center to foster continuous engagement, dialogue, and networking between India and its global diaspora.
It is the headquarters of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) handling foreign students.
It functions as a stock exchange exclusively for diaspora investments in Indian masala bonds.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Pravasi Bharatiya Kendra was established to provide a institutional platform for connecting with the diaspora, housing research facilities, cultural exhibitions, and interaction spaces to address diaspora concerns and celebrate their heritage.

practiceQuestions.q: Which policy measure has India increasingly adopted to protect vulnerable blue-collar migrant workers in West Asia?
opts: Complete ban on emigration of workers to all Gulf countries.
Implementation of the e-Migrate system, minimum referral wages, and bilateral labor agreements to ensure safe and legal migration.
Granting automatic Indian citizenship to all Gulf workers upon retirement.
Imposing heavy tariffs on oil imports from nations violating labor rights.
practiceQuestions.sol: To curb exploitation by unscrupulous agents, the government introduced the e-Migrate portal, making registration mandatory for recruitment agents and certain categories of emigrants (Emigration Check Required - ECR passport holders), coupled with Minimum Referral Wages (MRW) and MADAD portal for grievance redressal.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary significance of the 'Know India Programme' (KIP) run by the Ministry of External Affairs?
opts: To train foreign diplomats in Indian administrative services.
To familiarize diaspora youth (aged 18-30) with India's culture, heritage, and contemporary socio-economic development.
To provide financial grants to elderly diaspora members returning permanently to India.
To recruit top tech minds from Western universities into ISRO and DRDO.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Know India Programme (KIP) is a flagship initiative for diaspora engagement, targeting youth of Indian origin to promote awareness about India's progress, culture, and bonding with their motherland.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the classification and definition of the Indian Diaspora:
1. The Indian Diaspora comprises Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs), and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs).
2. PIO cardholders have identical political rights in India as Indian citizens, including the right to contest parliamentary elections.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. The Indian diaspora encompasses NRIs, PIOs (merged into OCI), and OCI cardholders. Statement 2 is incorrect because neither PIO nor OCI cardholders possess political rights in India; they cannot vote in elections or contest for parliamentary or state legislative seats.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Constitutional provisions related to Non-Resident Indians (NRIs):
1. Article 9 of the Indian Constitution states that persons voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign State shall cease to be citizens of India.
2. The Indian Constitution provides for dual citizenship for individuals residing in Commonwealth countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 9 explicitly mandates single citizenship by terminating Indian citizenship if a person acquires foreign nationality. Statement 2 is incorrect because India strictly follows a single citizenship model (Article 9 & 11) and does not permit dual citizenship for Commonwealth countries or any other nation.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Voting Rights for Overseas Indians:
1. The Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 2010 enabled Indian citizens living abroad due to work or education to vote in Indian elections.
2. Overseas electors can currently cast their votes electronically or via postal ballots from their foreign place of residence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The 2010 amendment introduced Section 20A, allowing NRIs to register on electoral rolls. Statement 2 is incorrect because while they can register as voters, they are still required to visit their respective polling booths in India physically to cast their votes; remote voting options (like postal or ETPBS) are currently not legally available to general NRI civilians.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) scheme:
1. An OCI cardholder is granted lifelong multiple-entry visa-free travel to India.
2. OCI cardholders require special permission from the government to undertake missionary, mountaineering, or research work in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because OCI cardholders still need a foreign passport along with their OCI registration booklet/card (lifelong multi-entry visa) to travel to India; it is not 'visa-free' travel, but rather an exemption from regular visa requirements. Statement 2 is correct: OCI cardholders must obtain prior permission from designated authorities for missionary, mountaineering, journalism, or research activities in India.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the economic significance of the Indian diaspora:
1. India is consistently among the top recipients of inward remittances globally, largely driven by diaspora workers in the Gulf and Western nations.
2. Remittances are classified as debt-creating capital inflows under India's capital account.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: India receives over $100 billion annually in remittances, ranking first globally. Statement 2 is incorrect because remittances are unilateral transfers recorded under the **Current Account**, not the Capital Account, and they are strictly **non-debt creating** inflows.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding institutional arrangements for the Indian diaspora:
1. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) is the nodal ministry handling all matters relating to Non-Resident Indians and Persons of Indian Origin.
2. The High-Level Committee on Indian Diaspora was chaired by L.M. Singhvi, whose recommendations led to the creation of the OCI scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Following the merger of the Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs (MOIA) into the MEA in 2016, the MEA handles all diaspora affairs. The L.M. Singhvi Committee (2002) recommended amending citizenship laws to accommodate dual nationality/OCI for the Indian diaspora.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding historical waves of the Indian diaspora:
1. The first major wave of Indian migration occurred during the British colonial period under the 'Girmitiya' (indentured labor) system to colonies like Fiji, Mauritius, and Trinidad.
2. Post-independence migration saw a significant outflow of highly skilled professionals, scientists, and engineers towards North America and Europe.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are historically accurate. The 19th-century indentured labor diaspora formed the bedrock of the diaspora in the Caribbean, Africa, and Pacific islands, while post-1960s migration was characterized by the 'brain drain' of technical professionals to the US, UK, and Canada.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding government initiatives for the welfare of the Indian diaspora:
1. The 'MADAD' portal has been established by the Ministry of External Affairs to help diaspora members lodge and track grievances regarding consular services.
2. The 'Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana' (PBBY) is a mandatory insurance scheme designed to protect emigrant workers going to ECR countries against accidental death, disability, and repatriation costs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The MADAD (Consular Grievance Monitoring System) portal enables grievance redressal for overseas Indians. PBBY provides vital social security, life insurance, and legal/medical aid to ECR (Emigration Check Required) passport holders traveling to West Asia and other notified countries.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of the Indian diaspora in India's foreign policy and diplomacy:
1. The Indian diaspora acts as an effective lobby group in foreign parliaments, influencing legislation and bipartisan support for India (e.g., during the India-US civil nuclear agreement).
2. Diaspora contributions are restricted solely to financial remittances and exclude technological or intellectual transfers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Indian diaspora in the US and other Western countries has played a pivotal role in lobbying for favorable strategic and economic policies toward India. Statement 2 is incorrect because diaspora engagement extends far beyond remittances; it includes massive intellectual capital transfers, scientific collaborations (e.g., VAJRA scheme), venture capital investments, and philanthropic engagements.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Citizenship (Amendment) Act and OCI cards:
1. The Central Government holds the statutory authority to cancel OCI registration under specific conditions such as disaffection towards the Constitution of India or fraud.
2. OCI cardholders possess the constitutional right to equality of opportunity in matters of public employment under Article 16 of the Indian Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Under Section 7D of the Citizenship Act, 1955, the Central Government can cancel OCI cards on grounds of fraud, disloyalty to the Constitution, or violation of any law. Statement 2 is incorrect because fundamental rights like Article 16 (equality of opportunity in public employment) and Article 15, 16, 19, 29, 30 are available **exclusively to citizens of India**, not to OCI cardholders who are foreign nationals.
